content:
incbot: INCIDENT ALERT: Autoscaler stalled in aws-us-central3 — sustained queue growth and GPU allocation failures. Paging oncall.
maya (oncall): ack. seeing big queue spike on the inference-router. latency > 3s 95p and token errors increasing. i’m taking lead.
raj (sre): on it. quick check — autoscaler reports repeated 403/QuotaExceeded from cloud API when requesting new GPU instances. not an internal scheduling failure yet.
jamie (infra): confirm — cloud quota for gpu_count in account "redwood-prod" region aws-us-central3 seems at hard cap. requests are being rejected at provider. logs show: 
```
2026-05-02T09:03:12Z autoscaler: request v1/instances create -> 403 QuotaExceeded: Requested GPUs (12) would exceed quota (12)
```
maya (oncall): that matches the surge pattern. queue keeps growing because autoscaler can't provision new nodes.
eli (eng-runtime): how many pending requests? are lower-priority/paying tiers affected?
maya (oncall): current queue ~4200 active requests across routes. Affected: high-throughput customers and background batching jobs. Top impacted: Acme (critical), OrbitHealth (prod sampling). we’re seeing increased 429s for some sharded endpoints.
leila (customer-sr): flagging Acme CSM and starting a short note to customers. will wait for a mitigation plan first. can we estimate hit to SLA?
raj (sre): rough numbers: 95p latency jumped from 0.8s -> 3.5s, error rate for generation endpoints up ~6% (from 0.2%). SLA exposures for customers with strict latency SLAs: Acme and OrbitHealth. i’ll quantify for comms.
jamie (infra): mitigation options:
- request expedited quota increase (submitted)
- spin up fallback instances in nearby region (aws-us-central2) and route traffic there
- run temporary model-fallback: auto-switch to smaller, quantized model variants for non-enterprise routes
- throttle/cut concurrency for background/backfill jobs
which do we want first?
maya (oncall): submit quota request now and do region failover for highest-priority traffic. eli, can runtime do model fallback automatically for low-tier traffic?
eli (eng-runtime): yes, we have a runtime policy to fallback to quantized-ggml variants. i can flip the flag for non-enterprise routes. that'll reduce GPU memory and allow smaller instance sizes.
jamie (infra): i’ll start region failover for critical customers only. commands:
```
# create ephemeral nodepool in us-central2 with smaller gpus
cloudctl compute nodepool create --region=aws-us-central2 --gpu=V100-small --count=8 --tag=ephemeral-incident-4805
# route Acme and OrbitHealth traffic to pool
infractl route update --route=acme-prod --to nodepool/ephemeral-incident-4805
```
maya (oncall): do we have capacity in us-central2? any quota there?
jamie (infra): yes, us-central2 quota free ~48 GPUs. ok to use. will start provisioning now.
raj (sre): also throttling background batchers to free up slots for real-time traffic. command pushed: 
```
kubectl scale deployment batchers --replicas=2 -n workloads
```
maya (oncall): quota request status?
jamie (infra): submitted an expedited ticket to AWS support: case # 987654321. ETA unknown but asked for immediate uplift for 48 GPUs. included telemetry and customer impact.
leila (customer-sr): drafting initial notification: short and honest. will send a 1-line to Acme now saying we’re actively mitigating; will update in 30m.
maya (oncall): runtime fallback flag is being toggled to reduce memory per model; eli confirm it's live when done.
eli (eng-runtime): done. non-enterprise routes are now on quantized fallback. expected per-request GPU memory down ~35% and token throughput slightly lower but more parallelism available.
maya (oncall): jamie — status on ephemeral pool provisioning?
jamie (infra): nodepool creation in progress, some boot failures but overall nodes coming up. 5/8 ready. routing live for Acme (manual override). monitoring edge latency now.
raj (sre): seeing a drop in queue for Acme route by ~40% after reroute and throttle. overall system queue down 18%.
maya (oncall): good. can we get a quick cost/quality note for customers? leila please hold a quick blurb: we switched to Q-model for some traffic; this may subtly change output distribution but will preserve correctness for most use cases.
leila (customer-sr): noted. sending update: "We’ve routed to an alternate region and engaged a reduced-precision model for certain low-priority requests to stabilize performance; core production traffic is being prioritized. We'll follow up with a full incident summary."
eli (eng-runtime): note — quantized fallback increases occasional tokenization edge cases. logging increased, but only affects lower-tier routes.
maya (oncall): continue monitoring. timeline:
- 09:03 incident detected
- 09:07 quotas confirmed blocked
- 09:09 fallback model enabled
- 09:12 region failover routing started
- 09:22 Acme queue reduced ~40%
- 09:30 throttles applied to background jobs
next actions: jamie continue bringing up remaining nodes in us-central2, raj keep throttles as needed, eli monitor quality regressions, leila coordinate customer comms. if quota uplift arrives, we can reprovision in region and shift back.
jamie (infra): update: ephemeral pool now 8/8 ready. routed additional customers off the blocked region. latency improving across the board.
raj (sre): autoscaler error rate for create requests is still high for aws-us-central3 — cloud still returning QuotaExceeded when attempted. we should disable autoscaler attempts in that region to avoid noise and redundant API calls.
maya (oncall): do that now. jamie?
jamie (infra): disabling autoscaler in aws-us-central3 for now. command: 
```
autoscalerctl set-region-enabled --region=aws-us-central3 --enabled=false
```
maya (oncall): good. also set alert suppression so we don't get paged repeatedly while mitigations are in place.
raj (sre): suppression applied for the autoscaler error alert group for 1 hour.
leila (customer-sr): sent Acme and OrbitHealth interim updates. both acknowledge and asked for ETA. told them 45–60m for stabilization.
maya (oncall): estimating recovery path: either quota uplift (variable) or keep traffic routed to fallback nodes until capacity normalizes. we'll plan to hand off to daytime oncall in 45 minutes once metrics stable.
eli (eng-runtime): logging summary prepared and will capture examples of model diffs for postmortem.
jamie (infra): cloud support replied — case #987654321 updated: awaiting internal review, no immediate uplift yet. they asked for usage justification and signed PO. we provided it.
raj (sre): cost note — ephemeral failover will incur cross-region costs. finance/ops FYI.
maya (oncall): nextcheck at +15m. any objections to keeping throttles and routing for 1 hour minimum?
leila (customer-sr): fine. customers prefer stability.
maya (oncall): ok moving to monitoring. handoff: if anything degrades beyond current levels, re-pager.
incbot: INCIDENT NOTE: handoff scheduled to daytime-oncall at 4805013600. Open actions: follow up with AWS case #987654321, prepare incident postmortem with model-fallback performance numbers, customer comms summary.
maya (oncall): closing this live thread for now — monitoring channel only. thanks team. :thumbsup:
